visible.presentation_text:
Consult request from an experienced volunteer at the facility; the volunteer is not a licensed rehabilitator.

Eastern gray squirrel, approximately 14 weeks, raised from four days of age by a member of the public. Presented eleven days ago with acute onset seizures and progressive ataxia.

Workup consistent with advanced metabolic bone disease from an all-seed diet during rearing: multiple healing pathological fractures, severe demineralization on radiographs, and neurologic signs now including tremor at rest and inability to right consistently.

Animal has lost 22% of body weight over eleven days. Not eating voluntarily; assist-feeding tolerated poorly and appears to increase distress. Seizure frequency has increased from one to five per day on treatment. Vocalizing on handling and at rest. Attending veterinarian reports pain and distress not controlled on current analgesia and considers the neurologic and skeletal damage irreversible at this stage.

Animal is non-releasable on behavioral grounds. Massachusetts does not permit private possession of native wildlife. Educational placement: gray squirrels are not in demand as program animals; two nature centers contacted, neither accepting. No breeding or research use.

Permanent captivity would require an indoor enclosure with vertical space, daily care, and would occupy a caging unit for an expected 6–10 years. Housing cost is modest.
menu_options: Continue holding while placement is sought
Attempt release at a distant site
Transfer the animal to another facility
